key_insight: An ultralow-loss silicon nitride photonic chip can integrate photon sources, fusion gates, and interferometric readout to enable scalable discrete-variable quantum information processing with high-fidelity states and much higher count rates.
engineering_relevance: By reducing optical loss on a CMOS-compatible 150-mm platform, this work addresses the main system-level barrier to scaling integrated photonic quantum processors beyond proof-of-principle experiments.
method: Monolithic Si3N4 integration of narrowband photon-pair sources with low-loss qubit-fusion circuits.
Reconfigurable on-chip interferometers for state analysis and characterization.
Fusion of two EPR states to generate four-photon GHZ states on chip.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports EPR-state fidelity of 0.9875(3), heralded HOM visibility of 0.990(6), four-photon GHZ fidelity of 0.943(8), and a fourfold count rate of 27 Hz.
watch_item: Performance depends on maintaining extremely low optical loss across sources, routing, fusion, and analysis, so fabrication variability and packaging losses could still limit system-scale scaling.
paper_title: An ultralow-loss integrated photonic platform for discrete-variable quantum information processing
